system.name: Parcelworks
system.summary: Parcels come in through intake, wait in a durable SQLite queue, and are claimed by a worker under a time-limited lease. The worker routes each one: book a carrier, park it on hold, or fail the attempt and retry with backoff. A report counts what happened.
system.purpose: A parcel is accepted once, gets a carrier label, and is counted as delivered in the report. Refusing, holding and failing for good are deliberate answers, not crashes.

stages.title: Intake
stages.blurb: A parcel request is checked, then refused or put in line.

stages.title: Queue
stages.blurb: Durable jobs in SQLite, claimed under a lease.

stages.title: Work
stages.blurb: The worker loop routes each claimed parcel.

stages.title: Retry and hold
stages.blurb: Backoff retries, terminal failure, and parked parcels.

stages.title: Report
stages.blurb: Counts outcomes and saves the report file.

boxes.title: Web client sends a parcel
boxes.plain: The web status client posts the parcel to /api/parcels and gets back an accepted receipt or a refused answer with a reason code. Server errors are retried 3 times, then thrown.
boxes.why: The only way a person outside the machine reaches intake.
boxes.failure: A 5xx answer is retried 3 times, then an Error is thrown

boxes.title: Take the submit request
boxes.plain: The submit command wraps intake. It answers ok with a receipt, or ok false with the refusal code and message. A refusal is an answer, not a crash.

boxes.title: Check required fields
boxes.plain: Id, sender, recipient, postcode and weight_g must all be present and non-empty. A zero weight counts as missing.

boxes.title: Check weight against limit
boxes.plain: The weight must be a positive whole number of grams and at most MAX_WEIGHT_G (30000 by default). Anything else is refused as bad_weight or overweight.
boxes.why: Keeps parcels the carrier cannot take out of the queue.

boxes.title: Check postcode and service
boxes.plain: The postcode must be 5 capital letters or digits. The service must be standard or express, and defaults to standard.

boxes.title: Look for a duplicate id
boxes.plain: accept asks the queue whether this parcel id already exists. A repeat id is refused and nothing is overwritten.

boxes.title: Choose the lane
boxes.plain: With FAST_LANE on, an express parcel of 500 g or less skips the queue. With it off, which is the default, every parcel takes the normal lane.

boxes.title: Record as done at intake
boxes.plain: The parcel is stored already done, with no carrier label and no worker involved. Used only when FAST_LANE=1.
boxes.why: Lets tiny express parcels skip the backlog.
outputs: a done job row with no label

boxes.title: Put the parcel in line
boxes.plain: The parcel is stored as a pending job and a normal-lane receipt is returned.

boxes.title: Parcel refused
boxes.plain: The caller gets the refusal code and message and nothing is stored. Codes: missing_field, bad_weight, overweight, bad_postcode, bad_service, duplicate.

boxes.title: Jobs waiting in line
boxes.plain: Each accepted parcel is a row in the jobs table with status pending. A job can be claimed once its available_at time has passed, which is how backoff delays work.

boxes.title: Claim the oldest ready job
boxes.plain: One transaction picks the oldest pending job that is ready and returns it, or returns nothing if no job is ready.
boxes.why: Only one worker can lease a given job at a time.
outputs: a Job with a lease token, or nothing

boxes.title: Job leased to a worker
boxes.plain: While leased, the job belongs to one worker until lease_until (LEASE_SECONDS, 30 by default). Claiming also adds one to its attempts. Only the holder of the lease token can complete, fail or hold it.

boxes.title: Reclaim expired leases
boxes.plain: Before every claim, jobs whose lease ran out go back in line, or are failed if they already used their last attempt. A crashed worker's job is not lost.
boxes.why: A worker that dies mid-job must not strand it.
boxes.failure: Out of attempts: the job is failed with 'lease expired on final attempt'

boxes.title: Mark the job done
boxes.plain: Marks a leased job done and stores its carrier label. It only works for the current lease token; a worker whose lease expired and was re-claimed gets False and drops its result.
boxes.failure: False when the lease token no longer matches

boxes.title: Finished jobs
boxes.plain: Done jobs stay in the table. The report counts them as delivered, and the web client's wait stops when it sees one.

boxes.title: Run the worker loop
boxes.plain: Ticks until a tick cap is reached or, with stop_when_idle, the queue is empty. Counts how many times each ending happened. A running service sets neither stop.

boxes.title: Run one job
boxes.plain: One pass: reclaim expired leases, claim a job, run the handler, then settle the attempt as done, held, retry, failed or lease_lost.
outputs: an ending name, or None when nothing was ready

boxes.title: Sleep while idle
boxes.plain: When nothing is ready the worker sleeps idle_s seconds and tries again. A job waiting out its backoff looks the same as an empty queue.

boxes.title: Route the parcel
boxes.plain: A declared value over the customs limit without cleared papers is parked, and so is a ZZ postcode. Everything else goes to the carrier.
outputs: a Verdict: label or hold reason

boxes.title: Book the carrier
boxes.plain: A pretend carrier call returns a label like LBL-pw-1. Outage-zone postcodes (99xxx) always raise TransientError.

boxes.title: Lease lost, work dropped
boxes.plain: The worker's lease was gone when it tried to settle, because another claim replaced it. Its result is thrown away so the job is not settled twice.

boxes.title: Record the failed attempt
boxes.plain: A TransientError counts as a failed attempt. With tries left (MAX_ATTEMPTS, 4 by default) the job returns to pending with a delay. Out of tries, it is failed for good.
boxes.why: Keeps a flaky carrier from losing parcels while still stopping a hopeless one.

boxes.title: Wait out the backoff
boxes.plain: The retry cannot be claimed until now plus base times 2 to the (attempt minus 1) seconds: 2, 4, 8 by default, capped at 300.

boxes.title: Terminal failure
boxes.plain: No tries left: the job is failed for good and the report counts it as a dead letter. Reached by the last failed attempt, or by a lease that expired on the last attempt.

boxes.title: Customs hold
boxes.plain: A declared value over CUSTOMS_LIMIT_CENTS (50000 by default) parks the job in hold. Only an operator's release request with paperwork moves it.
boxes.why: Customs paperwork arrives outside the system.
boxes.failure: Waits until a later release request arrives

boxes.title: Address hold
boxes.plain: A ZZ postcode parks the job in hold as an address hold. The release command answers still on hold for these, and no other code moves a job out of hold.
boxes.why: The region cannot be verified automatically.
boxes.failure: The web client's wait ends in PollTimeout for a held job

boxes.title: Release a customs hold
boxes.plain: A later operator request. A customs hold with paperwork given is released and marked cleared so routing lets it through. Without paperwork the answer is still on hold (customs).
outputs: released, or still on hold with the reason

boxes.title: Answer still on hold
boxes.plain: For an address hold the release command only answers still on hold (address) and changes nothing. No release is written for address holds.
outputs: ok false with the hold reason

boxes.title: Count parcels by outcome
boxes.plain: Counts done, failed and held jobs under their Outcome names: delivered, dead_letter, held. Jobs still pending or leased are not outcomes yet.
outputs: counts plus held, failed and delivered lists

boxes.title: Write the report text
boxes.plain: Lays the counts out as text: one row per outcome name, then lists of held parcels with their reason, dead letters with their last error, and delivered labels.

boxes.title: Save the report file
boxes.plain: Writes a temp file and swaps it into place. If that fails with an OS error it waits and tries again, with no cap on the number of tries.
boxes.failure: OSError sends it to the wait box

boxes.title: Wait and try again
boxes.plain: Sleeps min(2 to the attempt, 30) seconds, then loops back to the write. No attempt limit is written in the code.

boxes.title: Report saved
boxes.plain: The report path is returned to the caller.

boxes.title: Returned to sender
boxes.plain: An outcome name the report prints as a row, always 0. It is declared in Outcome, but no code sets a parcel to it.

loops.title: Retry with backoff
loops.blurb: A failed carrier call sends the job back to pending with a growing delay.
loops.limit: MAX_ATTEMPTS tries per job (4 by default), then terminal failure

loops.title: Worker loop
loops.blurb: Tick, claim, route, settle, tick again.
loops.limit: max_ticks or stop_when_idle; a running service sets neither

loops.title: Report write retry
loops.blurb: A busy destination makes the writer sleep and try the whole write again.

loops.title: Customs hold and release
loops.blurb: A release request either frees the job or leaves it on hold.
loops.limit: Each lap needs a new operator request

loops.title: Address hold and answer
loops.blurb: A release request is answered and the job stays on hold.
loops.limit: Each lap needs a new operator request

paths.title: Main path
paths.blurb: One ordinary parcel from request to saved report.

paths.title: Carrier outage to terminal failure
paths.blurb: An outage-zone parcel goes round the retry loop, waiting longer each lap, until MAX_ATTEMPTS and then fails for good.

paths.title: Customs hold and release
paths.blurb: A high-value parcel is parked until an operator sends a release with paperwork.

paths.title: Address hold
paths.blurb: A ZZ postcode is parked. A release request gets the answer still on hold, every time.

paths.title: Fast lane
paths.blurb: With FAST_LANE on, a small express parcel is stored as done at intake.

terms.meaning: A worker's time-limited ownership of a claimed job (LEASE_SECONDS, 30 by default). Only the holder of the lease token can settle it.
Take the oldest ready pending job and lease it, in one transaction.
The wait before a failed job may be claimed again: 2 s, doubling each try, capped at 300 s.
A job parked with a reason, customs or address, until an operator sends a release request.
The report's name for a job that was failed for good.
FAST_LANE: small express parcels are stored as done at intake. Off by default.
Postcodes starting 99, where the pretend carrier always fails.
One pass of the worker loop: process_one.
A settle attempt whose lease token no longer matches. The worker reports it as lease_lost.
The carrier booking code, like LBL-pw-1, stored with a done job.

end:web/client.ts::StatusClient.waitForT.why: the client gives up after POLL_LIMIT polls; the job itself is unaffected
